title: SLO escrow transfer and cascading graceful-fallback procedure for regional model endpoints
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Problem: We need an operational procedure to move error budget between regional model endpoints during prolonged incidents, and a deterministic cascading fallback that preserves high-priority traffic while avoiding global service collapse. This ticket defines SLI measurements, SLO escrow transfer rules, circuit-breaker thresholds, and staged load-shedding slices for per-endpoint/model routes.
slis: Availability SLI: proportion of successful 2xx responses for route X measured at the model endpoint (per-region, 5m rolling window). Exclude known client errors (4xx).
Latency SLI: P95 tail of server-side token latency for generation endpoints, measured per-route and per-variant over 1h windows.
Quality SLI: semantic-quality pass rate using the canonical promptset (synthetic eval) run hourly; used only for guarded degradation of model variants.
Queueing SLI: fraction of requests that experience queue wait > policy threshold (250ms) at ingress prior to batching.
Error Rate SLI: percentage of 5xx responses and stream interruption events per route per region (1h aggregated).
slo_policy: Default SLOs: Availability >= 99.5% monthly, Latency P95 <= 600ms for low-latency routes. Tiered overrides for premium customers (99.9% / 350ms).
SLO windows: primary enforcement window is 30 days for budgeting; short probation window of 72 hours for emergency transfers.
SLO ownership: endpoints declare SLOs in endpoint manifest; runtime enforces and reports burn rates to the SLO arbiter service.

Escrow principle: reserve up to 10% of monthly error budget per-region as an escrow pool that can be transferred into neighboring regions under defined conditions. Transfers are temporary and time-limited.
Transparency: escrow transfers, estimated remaining budget and transfer amortization must be visible in the Console SLO dashboard and included in incident runbooks.
error_budget_mechanism: Trigger for escrow transfer: a region's burn rate > 4x for 30m AND sustained controller-level CPU/GPU pressure > 70% AND neighboring region has >=2x spare budget available.
Transfer unit: transfers express as 'slo-minutes' (minutes of SLO credit) to make cross-region math uniform across latency/availability SLOs.
Duration: transferred escrow is active for a probation window (default: 6 hours) then decays linearly back to the home-region unless renewed by the SLO arbiter.
Rollback: if the receiving region's error budget reach burn > 3x after transfer, automatic retract (partial) occurs and traffic is scaled back to the original routing via the fallback plan.
Auditing: every transfer writes an immutable record with cause, initiator (automatic/manual), metrics snapshot, and amortization schedule to the audit log (KMS-signed).
failover_procedure: Level 0 (Graceful): auto-route non-user-facing batch/async traffic to standby region using weighted-balance delta of 20% increments, preserving pinning for P0 customers.
Level 1 (Escalation): activate escrow transfer to neighboring healthy region and increase allowed token latency budget for non-critical routes by one degradation tier.
Level 2 (Cascading fallback): invoke pre-warm standby variants with lower-cost quantized models in receiving region and shift traffic in 10% steps while monitoring quality SLI and tail latency.
Manual override: SRE on-call can force failover with `--hard` flag if safety checks fail to reduce error burn in 30 minutes; this must be followed by post-action review.
De-escalation: reverse traffic movements only after both: (a) originating region burn rate < 1.2x baseline for 2h, and (b) KV cache warming reach >= 70% hit rate or acceptable latency restored.
circuit_breaker_config: Per-route tokenized breakers: open if 5xx rate > 1.5% AND error burn rate > 2x baseline for 15m. While open, return structured fallback augmentation (informational header + reduced-size response).
Graceful degrade mode: when breaker is half-open, route 25% of traffic to canary variant; increase to 50%/75% before full close if quality SLI remains stable.
Multi-region coordination: breakers propagate tags across regions to avoid thrashing; breaker state is soft-cached for 1 minute with conflict resolution favoring higher-severity state.
Backoff policy: exponential backoff window starts at 30s, doubles up to 20 minutes. Alerts escalate on each backoff step.
load_shedding_rules: Priority slices: mark tokens into slices: premium, standard, bulk. When capacity is constrained, bulk traffic is shed first, then standard, preserving premium within SLO allocation.
Token-aware shedding: prefer shedding long-running requests that consume > X tokens predicted (heuristic) to maximize short-response throughput.
Soft-shed strategy: for chat sessions, replace full generation with summary-only responses when dropping behind SLA targets for standard/bulk slices.
Fallback content policy: any served soft-shed response must include a machine-readable header providing degrade_reason and expected confidence delta.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Spec review): share this doc with PM, Security, and Runtime leads for 1-week review. Link to draft artifacts in Links below.
Phase 2 (Simulation): run chaos tests in staging that simulate region CPU/GPU pins, verify transfer/retract under 100 synthetic routes over 48h.
Phase 3 (Canary): enable escrow transfers in canary region for 2 weeks with monitoring and manual approval gate for global enablement.
Phase 4 (GA): after 3 successful canary incidents, flip default escrow policy to auto with conservative thresholds; iterate on knobs based on observed false positives.
testing_plan: Unit tests for SLO-arbiter logic (transfer calculus, decay schedule).
Integration test: end-to-end with routing controller and console visibility hooks.
Chaos experiment: unilateral region outage, validate no global collapse, measure time to recover and number of transfer/retract events.
Load test: synthetic token-heavy traffic to exercise token-aware shedding heuristics and verify preserved P95 latency for premium slice.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: per-region SLO burn chart, escrow pool size, active transfers, and amortization timeline.
Alerts: PagerDuty if transfer initiated AND originating region burn rate still > 3x after 30m.
Audit stream: log transfer events to compliance pipeline (retention 1y) and surface in Console timeline.
SLO Arbiter signals: expose metrics for 'transfer-confidence' and 'retract-risk' to guide manual operator decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Automated escrow transfer calculations implemented in SLO arbiter and covered by unit tests.
End-to-end integration demonstrates transfer + retract in staging without customer-visible errors for premium slice.
Console surfaces transfer records and amortization timelines for operators.
SRE runbook updated with explicit rollback steps and post-incident checklist.

notes: Design decision: use 'slo-minutes' to avoid disparate currency conversions between latency and availability SLOs — simplifies amortization and operator reasoning.
Operational constraint: KV-cache warming is the most common blocker for fast reversal; adding an explicit warm-up probe improves de-escalation safety.
Risk: mis-tuned automatic transfers could accelerate burn in healthy regions; mitigations include conservative defaults, canary gating, and per-tenant caps.
